title: 60% off Powerguard 3000 Watt Portable Power Station (2560wh) $1279.60 (RRP $3199) Delivered @ Techunion
body:
Deal: 60% off Powerguard 3000 Watt Portable Power Station (2560wh) $1279.60 (RRP $3199) Delivered @ Techunion

[FLICKIT] There's some info in the comments on the last deal: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/comment/17638343/redir
Edit: and there's a user manual (with specs) down the page here: https://powerguard.com.au/products/powerguard-power-station-…
[skysurfer] Couldn't see the user manusl. Saw my own comment on the last deal though, asking for the specs, wasn't answered then either.
[POWERGUARDAU] Here's a link to the user manual for full details.
https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0756/1471/6201/files/PGPS3…
[ShadowSaver] Op, if there are any warranty issues, who covers the return postage? Also, if return postage is not covered by TechUnion, can we drop the item off at a location in each state instead?
[POWERGUARDAU] Any valid warranty returns will be arranged via Tech Union freight company to their service centre. You would need to book through Tech Union customer service team. We do this as the unit is too heavy for Australia Post. Big Capacity unit at 2.56KWh.
[foobar] So … just to clarify, "who covers the return postage" is what was asked, and the answer is "valid warranty returns will be arranged via Tech Union freight company", which means you / they cover shipping?
I'm interested in getting a unit, perhaps two, but can't find any reviews, can't even see a weight in your website specs, the price on the website seems to be a grand more than the RRP you mention here which tracks as the price you've listed is 40% of 3199 not 2199.
What's the return rate, percentage wise?
Are the warranty terms clearly laid out somewhere? Is it warrantied on capacity loss, if so, how much over what time etc? What brand cells does it use and what grade are they?
Seems to be a LOT of relevant and important details missing.
[POWERGUARDAU] The weight of this unit is 34kg, so the trolley handle and wheels are super helpful.
As far as warranty returns we need to establish a valid issue and need to return. Once that is done through customer service Tech Union will cover the cost of returning the unit via freight, not post due to weight.
For more details on the unit you can go to the manufacturers site.
https://powerguard.com.au/collections/powerguard-portable-po…
As far as back up and support, Powerguard has been selling products in Australia for 35 years. Not too many of the competitors in this category could say that.
Will correct RRP in title as it is $3199. Thanks for pointing this out.
[joedante] They love to dodge answers, to the point I assume AI is doing some of the work because AI loves to add irrelevant nonsense.
When asked "Will you directly, without PR speak, say this is not a Biginverter SR3000?" on the last deal their answer was "I have not done a deep dive feature comparison on the two units so I cannot say. There are many Power Stations on the market so, best to choose the one with the feature set that suits your needs and budget. We stand on our committment to providing excellent customer service and products at a great price."
Because they have identical specs and look identical I'm pretty sure that non-answer is "yes, it's a generic product from alibaba we've slapped our name on".
The weird part is that's fine. It's fine to do that. Provide the local warranty, you're adding value, fair enough. But the inability to admit it and the ducking and weaving around questions makes you wonder what dealing with returns will be like.
https://www.alibaba.com/product-detail/BIGINVERTER-SR3000-30…
[changot] Interesting find from the previous deal comments.. Someone linked what looks like the same 3000W / 2560Wh unit from CE-LINK https://www.ce-link.com/products/3000W%20Portable%20Power%20… , plus a TechWalls review/teardown of the CE-LINK version. https://www.techwalls.com/ce-link-3000w-power-station-teardo…
The specs and design look very similar to the PowerGuard PGPS3000.
Can the PowerGuard rep confirm whether this is the same underlying CE-LINK model/platform, just configured for the Australian market and branded PowerGuard?
If so, that would actually be useful info for buyers because the TechWalls teardown gives a better look at the internals/build quality than the current PowerGuard reviews available.
Also curious if anyone here has owned the PowerGuard version since the earlier June/July deals and can share real-world feedback on battery performance, fan noise, app reliability, solar charging and warranty/support.
[changot] @POWERGUARDAU
Can you confirm who manufactures the PGPS3000 hardware, and whether it’s based on the CE-LINK / same ODM platform mentioned in the previous deal?
Also, if known, what brand/grade LiFePO4 cells are used?
No issue with ODM at all I'm just trying to understand exactly what’s inside the unit.
[MasterScythe] Does this have TOU to offset peak power costs in a unit?
Does it have solar Priority, even when AC connected?
What is the phantom draw of each type of output?
